title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All directors of Iress, including the Chair. Distinguished only for Trading Window approval: a director other than the Chair needs the Chair's written approval; the Chair needs approval from the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee (or, if unavailable, the Chair of the People and Performance Committee). Otherwise subject to the same insider trading, short-term dealing, short-selling, margin lending and hedging/derivatives rules as other tiers, plus a subsequent ASX-notification duty.

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: Direct reports of the Managing Director & CEO; the Company Secretary; the General Counsel APAC; the General Counsel EMEA; the Deputy CFO; the Head of Group Tax and Financial Control; direct reports of those positions; and other employees nominated as Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Employee
tiers.description: Employees and contractors of Iress who are not Directors or Restricted Persons. Subject to Trading Windows and the insider trading, short-term dealing, short-selling and hedging/derivatives rules, but not to the prior written approval requirement or the margin lending ban, which are limited to Directors and Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: Family members, trusts, companies, nominees and other persons over whom a director or employee has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on any derivative over Iress equity in any security state (expressly including minimum-shareholding-requirement shares, restricted vested equity rights, and unvested equity), with no Trading Window, clearance or exceptional-circumstances carve-out. Breach triggers cancellation/clawback of any unvested or restricted equity involved.

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Iress Securities subject to a minimum shareholding requirement are expressly included within the scope of the hedging/derivatives ban (5.4); the policy does not address whether hedged shares would be excluded from counting toward the MSR, since hedging them is banned outright.

exemption_authority: Trading outside a Trading Window may be approved only in rare exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or compliance with a court order; a tax bill alone does not qualify), by the Chair (for directors), the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee (for the Chair), or the Company Secretary (for employees/contractors); each approval is valid for a single application only and the approved Trade must occur within 3 business days unless withdrawn earlier. No exemption authority reaches the absolute bans on derivatives/hedging (5.4), margin lending/secured financing (5.3), short selling (5.2) or short-term dealing (5.1) - no clearance, waiver or exceptional-circumstances route is available for those.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The use of derivatives or any other hedging instrument over Iress equity ... is prohibited and those entering into such schemes will be in breach of the terms and conditions of the grant. As a consequence, the Board will exercise its right to cancel / clawback the hedged unvested or restricted equity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an unconditional ban reaching every tier and every security state, with a clawback penalty attached to unvested or restricted equity; it leaves no structural path for either leg of a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban has no clearance route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Iress Securities ... or grant lenders any rights over Iress Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that allow margin/secured lending subject to company consent, IRE bans it outright for Directors and Restricted Persons with no clearance mechanism at all, so the loan leg cannot be structured for those tiers regardless of the collar's economics; the ban is not stated to extend to plain employees, though the separate 5.4 derivatives ban would still block their collar's option legs.

bespoke_clauses.topic: minimum shareholding requirement named in the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: The use of derivatives or any other hedging instrument over Iress equity (including Iress Securities subject to a minimum shareholding requirement ...) is prohibited
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shows the Board specifically anticipated and shut down the argument that MSR-mandated holdings could be hedged while nominally satisfying the requirement.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Associate coverage may not extend to the margin lending ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement ... (clause 5.3, no reference to Associates, contrasted with clause 2.2 which expressly extends approval requirements to 'Directors and Restricted Persons (and their Associates)')
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clause 5.3's text does not repeat the Associate extension used elsewhere in the policy, creating textual ambiguity as to whether a family trust or company associated with a Director could enter a secured facility, though the general clause 1.1 statement that the whole policy applies to Associates would likely be read to close this gap.

bespoke_clauses.topic: refusal confidentiality runs the other way
bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to trade is refused, you must keep that information confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The confidentiality obligation on a refused approval binds the individual, not just the Company, which is relevant to how a bank counterparty could be told about a declined clearance.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any tier. Clause 5.4 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on 'the use of derivatives or any other hedging instrument over Iress equity' in any security state, with no Trading Window, clearance or exceptional-circumstances carve-out anywhere in the policy, and breach triggers cancellation/clawback of unvested or restricted equity - so neither the purchased put nor the written call can be entered into by a director, Restricted Person, employee or their Associate. Clause 5.3 separately and absolutely bans Directors and Restricted Persons from any margin loan or 'similar funding arrangement' to acquire Iress Securities, or from granting a lender any rights over Iress Securities, with no consent or clearance pathway at all (unlike many peer policies that permit margin lending with company consent), so the loan leg is independently prohibited for those tiers; this specific ban is not expressly extended to plain employees or to Associates, though the 5.4 derivatives ban still blocks the option legs for everyone regardless. Even ordinary share sales are confined to the four-week Trading Windows following full-year results, half-year results and the AGM (subject to Board variation) and, for Directors and Restricted Persons, prior written approval valid for only 3 business days - but none of this machinery offers any route around the absolute prohibitions in section 5.
